prerequisites: Fundamental concepts of Materials Science I (phase diagrams, crystalline structures, imperfections, and basic mechanical tests)
Basic notions of Chemistry and Physics from the first year of the degree

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Collaborate proactively in the development of work, setting goals and meeting objectives.
Contribute to finding solutions to challenges or projects, demonstrating empathy and assertiveness when sharing ideas, reflections, and arguments within collaborative work.
Structure discourse to facilitate understanding of the objectives, actions, and/or results of one's own work.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.

syllabus_topics: Obtaining and Processing of Ceramics. Powder Metallurgy
teaching_methods: Expository class (Participative lecture, conferences, company visits, attendance at fairs, etc.)
Participative class (Individual or in group. Case resolution, role-playing, technical application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates, etc.)
Laboratory (Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.)
Integrated project (Completion of a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.)

Tutoring (Personalized and small group attention. Instruction carried out with the objective of reviewing, redirecting class materials, learning, and carrying out assignments, etc. Specific student queries. Scheduled tutorials.)

assessment_methods.method: Written test (open-response test and objective test)
Resolution and co-evaluation of individual exercises and group problems

assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by weighting written tests at 70% and practice reports/problems at 30%. It is an indispensable condition to obtain a minimum average mark of 4 in the written tests to average with the exercises/reports/practices and with the Integrated Project. The subject will be considered passed if the final mark is equal to or greater than 5 points and none of the marks for the parts is less than 4 points. Students will have 2 annual calls per subject and course to pass the written exam.
